## github
The GitHub MCP Server provides tools to interact with GitHub platform.

Tool selection guidance:
	1. Use 'list_*' tools for broad, simple retrieval and pagination of all items of a type (e.g., all issues, all PRs, all branches) with basic filtering.
	2. Use 'search_*' tools for targeted queries with specific criteria, keywords, or complex filters (e.g., issues with certain text, PRs by author, code containing functions).

Context management:
	1. Use pagination whenever possible with batches of 5-10 items.
	2. Use minimal_output parameter set to true if the full information is not needed to accomplish a task.

Tool usage guidance:
	1. For 'search_*' tools: Use separate 'sort' and 'order' parameters if available for sorting results - do not include 'sort:' syntax in query strings. Query strings should contain only search criteria (e.g., 'org:google language:python'), not sorting instructions. Always call 'get_me' first to understand current user permissions and context. ## Issues

Check 'list_issue_types' first for organizations to use proper issue types. Use 'search_issues' before creating new issues to avoid duplicates. Always set 'state_reason' when closing issues. ## Pull Requests

PR review workflow: Always use 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'create' to create a pending review, then 'add_comment_to_pending_review' to add comments, and finally 'pull_request_review_write' with method 'submit_pending' to submit the review for complex reviews with line-specific comments.

Before creating a pull request, search for pull request templates in the repository. Template files are called pull_request_template.md or they're located in '.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE' directory. Use the template content to structure the PR description and then call create_pull_request tool.

2	# over the queue. ONE RUN PERFORMS ONE ITEM (§15.22), and the queue drains as a
3	# chain of runs: the scheduler run dispatches this workflow every hour, a run that settled
4	# its item dispatches the next, and the continuation job below covers a run that
5	# died before it could. It carries NO cron of its own — the scheduler run's hourly dispatch
6	# is the guaranteed delivery, so a lost `task:ready` label event is latency lost
7	# and never work lost.
8	#
9	# THIS IS THE ONLY PLACE SECRETS LIVE (DESIGN §14). The wiring converge stamps
10	# every task's declared `required_secrets`, plus each configured invocation
11	# endpoint's token secret, into the step env below by name — the scheduler run and the
12	# janitor get none, because they never execute task code. Code-work is the only task
13	# code that ever sees a value; the agent hop carries nothing.
14	#
15	# MORE CAPACITY IS MORE EXECUTORS. Nothing enumerates them and each claim is
16	# independently leased, so a second job, a matrix width, or a runner outside
17	# Actions entirely all work — the executor's whole interface is issue read/write
18	# plus the repo at HEAD.
19	name: Claudinite executor
20	
21	on:
22	  issues:
23	    types: [labeled]
24	  workflow_dispatch:
25	    inputs:
26	      continuation_depth:
27	        description: 'How many dead runs this chain has continued through — set by the continuation job below, never by hand'
28	        required: false
29	        type: string
30	
31	permissions:
32	  contents: write
33	  issues: write
34	  pull-requests: write
35	  actions: write
36	
37	jobs:
38	  execute:
39	    # A label event on anything else is not this workflow's business — and a
40	    # workflow_dispatch carries no label at all, so it always runs.
41	    # BOTH READY SPELLINGS, for as long as any fielded engine writes the legacy one
42	    # (#1119). A workflow's event trigger names label strings LITERALLY — nothing
43	    # here decodes — so this list is the one place the migration's two vocabularies
44	    # must both appear, and dropping the legacy spelling early makes every item an
45	    # older engine readies wait for the hourly scheduler run instead of starting now.
46	    if: >-
47	      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'
48	      || github.event.label.name == 'task:status:waiting-for-executor'
49	      || github.event.label.name == 'task:ready'
50	      || github.event.label.name == 'task:urgent'
51	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
52	    # The old cap — ≤ the engine's executing leash — retired with the heartbeat
53	    # (§15.15). A run is bounded by ONE work step now, and a holder that is alive
54	    # says so on its item every 15 minutes, so the leash reclaims silence rather
55	    # than length. What is left here is a backstop against a wedged runner, well
56	    # clear of any declared `code_work_timeout`.
57	    timeout-minutes: 350
58	    steps:
59	      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
60	      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
61	        with:
62	          node-version: 24
63	      - name: Pick up and execute ready work
64	        env:
65	          GITHUB_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
66	          # The operator hold (DESIGN §8): set this repo variable to `true` and
67	          # every entry point exits at its first act, having fired nothing.
68	          CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL: ${{ vars.CLAUDINITE_TASKS_SUSPEND_ALL }}
69	          # The wiring converge stamps every declared required_secret, and every
70	          # configured invocation endpoint's token, below this marker — by name.
71	          # claudinite:secrets
72	          CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.CCR_ROUTINE_TOKEN }}
73	        run: node .claudinite/shared/engine/scheduler/queue/executor.mjs
74	
75	  # A run that dies — crash, timeout, cancellation, runner loss — never reaches
76	  # its own re-dispatch, so without this the queue would sit until the next cron
77	  # fire. The platform runs this job on a FRESH runner after any such death
78	  # (DESIGN §10, S36), and its one step fires that dispatch instead: the
79	  # remainder drains in ~a minute, while the dead run's OWN item waits for the
80	  # executing leash to reclaim it — nothing here touches that item.
81	  #
82	  # `continuation_depth` is the stop. A run that dies at startup — a broken
83	  # engine, a revoked token — dies identically every time, and an unguarded
84	  # continuation would dispatch itself for as long as that lasts. After three the
85	  # chain stops and SAYS SO on the repo's workflow-failure issue: a queue that has
86	  # quietly stopped draining is the one failure nothing else here would surface,
87	  # since every individual run looks like an ordinary death.
88	  continue-the-chain:
89	    needs: execute
90	    if: failure() || cancelled()
91	    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
92	    permissions:
93	      actions: write
94	      issues: write
95	    steps:

97	        with:
98	          script: |
99	            const depth = Number('${{ inputs.continuation_depth }}' || 0) + 1;
100	            const ref = context.payload.repository?.default_branch
101	              ?? context.ref.replace('refs/heads/', '');
102	            const run = `${context.serverUrl}/${context.repo.owner}/${context.repo.repo}/actions/runs/${context.runId}`;
103	            if (depth <= 3) {
104	              await github.rest.actions.createWorkflowDispatch({
105	                owner: context.repo.owner,
106	                repo: context.repo.repo,
107	                workflow_id: 'claudinite-executor.yml',
108	                ref,
109	                inputs: { continuation_depth: String(depth) },
110	              });
111	              core.info(`the executor run died — dispatched a fresh one on ${ref} (continuation ${depth} of 3)`);
112	              return;
113	            }
114	            // The chain has died three times running: this is not one bad runner,
115	            // and dispatching a fourth would spend the day proving it. Escalate to
116	            // the same one-open-issue surface the scheduler's own failures use, and
117	            // let the hourly scheduler run be what tries again.
118	            const { owner, repo } = context.repo;
119	            const title = 'Claudinite executor chain failed repeatedly';
120	            // The platform reporting its own failure IS an origin (`task:origin:github`),
121	            // and a chain that has died three times is a break to diagnose — the
122	            // `failure` park, the one lane that holds a task's lane (#1119).
123	            const labels = ['workflow-failure', 'task:origin:github', 'task:status:needs-human-failure'];
124	            const ensure = [
125	              { name: 'workflow-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite scheduler: a scheduler run or task failed' },
126	              { name: 'task:origin:github', color: 'd4c5f9', description: 'Claudinite queue: filed by the platform itself — a workflow reporting its own failure' },
127	              { name: 'task:status:needs-human-failure', color: 'b60205', description: 'Claudinite queue: parked — the run broke, diagnose and fix' },
128	            ];
129	            for (const l of ensure) await github.rest.issues.createLabel({ owner, repo, ...l }).catch(() => {});
130	            const body = `Three consecutive executor runs died before finishing their item. The chain stops here; the next hourly scheduler run will dispatch a fresh one.\n\nThe last run: ${run}`;
131	            const found = await github.rest.search.issuesAndPullRequests({ q: `repo:${owner}/${repo} is:issue is:open in:title "${title}"` });
132	            if (found.data.total_count > 0) await github.rest.issues.createComment({ owner, repo, issue_number: found.data.items[0].number, body });
133	            else await github.rest.issues.create({ owner, repo, title, labels, body });

content.content:
# claudinite-tasks — scheduled work

Everything whose subject is task work: the work-item queue, the executor, the task contract and
its signals, calendar/anchor math, run records, code-work, and the delivery lane a task's output
lands through. Declaring this pack is what gives a repo scheduled work; a repo that does not
declare it runs none, which is a supported state rather than a degraded one.

The mechanism itself — the state machine, the generator, the executor's protocol, urgency and
forcing, recovery — is the canon's own tasks-dispatch design document, and authoring a task is the
`writing-tasks` skill's subject. This file is the pack's own map.

## Layout

| Path | What lives there |
|---|---|
| `queue/` | the work item and its vocabulary, the scheduler run, the executor and its continuation, the drain, leases, readiness, the janitor's rules, the schedule board, workflow-failure escalation |
| `queue/tasks/` | the built-in tasks (`implement-request`) |
| `signals/` | the signal collectors a precondition is handed |
| `stubs/` | the two workflow files an adopting repo receives |
| `shared-code/` | the published import surface — see below |
| `tasks/` | this pack's own scheduled tasks: `task-janitor` (the queue's sweeps) and `usage-fold` (it folds this mechanism's run records and outcome labels) |
| `worldRules/` | the task-declaration checks |
| `test/` | the unit suite, and `test/sim/` — the simulator and its scenario suite, the mechanism's executable spec |
| `executor.md`, `queue/instructions.md`, `deliver-pr.md` | operational documents a member's routines and workers read out of their own mount at runtime |

## `shared-code/` — the one sanctioned cross-pack import

Another pack's code may import `packs/claudinite-tasks/shared-code/*`, and nothing else of this
pack. The `pack-independence` barrier's allow list names that directory; no other pack gains an
equivalent surface by existing.

| Module | What it publishes | Who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| `work-items.mjs` | the title grammar that is a work item's identity, the outcome/status decode over its labels, lease state, the dispatch vocabulary, and what a scheduler run would instantiate | claudinite-dashboard, claudinite-fleet-sheepdog |
| `anchors.mjs` | period length, and the instant a task's window last opened at or opens next | claudinite-dashboard |
| `delivery.mjs` | `landPr`, `deliverGenerated` — how a task's output becomes a landed PR or a regenerated file | any pack whose tasks deliver |
| `github.mjs` | the GitHub client and REST helpers, and the tracker issue a worker records on | any pack whose tasks reach GitHub |
| `signals.mjs` | the signal shapes a precondition is handed | packs asserting what their own tasks will see |
| `task-contract.mjs` | task-declaration validation, and precondition evaluation as the executor does it | every pack with tasks, in its own tests |
| `usage-format.mjs` | the usage aggregate's codec | claudinite-fleet-sheepdog's fleet-wide aggregator |

A pack whose **non-task** code reads any of these declares `requires: ['claudinite-tasks']`. A
pack's `tasks/` folder needs no declaration: a mount without this pack carries no `tasks/` at all,
since a task folder is inert without the queue that runs it.

## Adoption

The two workflow files and the routine endpoints cannot converge into place — `.github/workflows/`
is the one directory a member's nightly update may never write — so they are scaffolded once, at
adoption, by the `adopt-pack` skill. They are static from then on: the per-repo cron minute and
anchor hours are written once, secrets travel as one fixed line, and the `run:` lines name mount
pack paths behind which everything converges nightly.

## The legacy `engine/scheduler/` shims

Until #1317's execution chain finishes, `engine/scheduler/*` still exists as one-line re-exports of
this pack, for members whose vendored workers, workflow `run:` lines and stored routine prompts
still name the old paths. They ship only into a mount that carries this pack, and they are deleted
once no fielded member names one.

1	// APPLYING a status transition — the write half of the vocabulary whose read half
2	// is `work-item.mjs`'s decode (tasks-dispatch DESIGN §4, the migration of #1119).
3	//
4	// One rule, and it is why this is not a plain `swapLabel`: the item may wear ANY
5	// engine version's spelling of the status it is leaving. A member's items outlive
6	// its converges, so an item filed as `task:ready` is picked up by an engine that
7	// writes `task:status:waiting-for-executor`, and a swap that named one spelling
8	// would leave the other standing — an item wearing two live statuses, which is the
9	// torn state the janitor exists to repair.
10	//
11	// Writes stay granular (add and remove named labels, never a set-write): with
12	// several executors and a scheduler run moving labels at once, a set-write from a
13	// stale snapshot clobbers a concurrent transition (DESIGN §4).
14	// The removes are UNCONDITIONAL — every spelling of the status being left, not
15	// only the ones the caller's snapshot shows. A caller holds the labels it read
16	// before its own earlier transitions, so filtering on that snapshot would skip
17	// exactly the label this engine just wrote; removing a label an issue does not
18	// carry 404s, which is the end state asked for and therefore success.
19	import { spellingsOf } from './work-item.mjs';
20	
21	// Move `item` out of `fromStatus` (canonical — every spelling of it goes) and into
22	// the label `to`, which is whatever spelling this engine writes.
23	export async function swapStatus(api, gh, repo, item, fromStatus, to) {
24	  await clearStatus(api, gh, repo, item, fromStatus);
25	  return api.addLabel(gh, repo, item.number, to);
26	}
27	
28	// Leave a status without entering another — the close path, where the terminal
29	// label is applied separately.
30	export async function clearStatus(api, gh, repo, item, status) {
31	  for (const label of spellingsOf(status)) {
32	    await api.removeLabel(gh, repo, item.number, label);
33	  }
34	}

1	// The machine-readable records a task's execution leaves in an Actions log
2	// (skill-usage-metrics DESIGN §4.2), and the parsers that read them back.
3	//
4	// TWO FAMILIES, ONE OF THEM HISTORICAL. `claudinite-task-run` was the SLOT
5	// scheduler's own line, one per due task per run; the slot scheduler is retired
6	// (#974) and nothing writes that line any more. The parser stays, and only the
7	// parser: Actions logs from before the retirement are still inside their retention
8	// window, and the usage fold still counts them. Nothing new should be taught this
9	// shape — `claudinite-task-exec` below is the live record.
10	//
11	// The counts these produce are exact within the Actions log retention window, and
12	// that is worth stating next to the capture-derived counts they land beside.
13	
14	// The five things a slot scheduler run could do with a due task. One name per
15	// outcome, used verbatim as the counter key in the aggregate, so there is no
16	// mapping table between "what the run said" and "what the fold counted" to drift.
17	export const TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze([
18	  // A dispatch issue was filed: an agent session ran this task.
19	  'agent',
20	  // The task ran with NO agent — an `agent_model: none` task (code-work is the
21	  // whole task), or an agentful one whose code-work requested no agent phase.
22	  // Kebab, not the declaration field's `code_work`: this word is a WIRE token,
23	  // constrained to the line format's `[a-z-]+` charset.
24	  'code-work',
25	  // Due, but its precondition said there was nothing to do.
26	  'skipped',
27	  // Its code-work failed; the run converged the task to a needs-human issue.
28	  'failed',
29	  // Due and past its precondition, but no NEW agent run started: this slot was
30	  // already dispatched (exactly-once), an earlier dispatch is still open
31	  // (at-most-one-open), or another task claimed the run exclusively. Work that
32	  // was wanted and did not happen this run.
33	  'deferred',
34	]);
35	
36	// An empty per-task counter row — every outcome present, zeros included, so a row's
37	// shape never depends on which outcomes a task happened to hit.
38	export const emptyTaskRun = () => Object.fromEntries(TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.map((o) => [o, 0]));
39	
40	// The line format. `v1` is the shape's version: a reader that meets a `v2` line
41	// knows it is looking at something it was not written for, instead of silently
42	// half-parsing it.
43	export const TASK_RUN_TAG = 'claudinite-task-run';
44	const VERSION = 'v1';
45	
46	// Actions stamps every log line with its own timestamp before the command's output,
47	// so the parse tolerates that prefix — without it, a fetched log reads as having
48	// printed nothing at all.
49	const LINE_RE = new RegExp(
50	  String.raw`^(?:\S+\s+)?${TASK_RUN_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
51	);
52	
53	// One line → `{ pack, task, slotId, outcome }`, or null for anything that is not a
54	// record of this version. Deliberately strict: an unknown outcome word is NOT a
55	// record, because counting it would mint a counter key nothing ever reads.
56	// The code phase has been renamed twice, and job logs outlive both renames:
57	// `preprocess` (pre-2026-08-06) and `prework` (pre-2026-08-18) are the earlier
58	// words for what is now `code-work`. Runs logged under either still parse, each
59	// normalized straight to the canonical word.
60	// Exported because the outcome words are also the usage aggregate's counter KEYS,
61	// and that file holds rows written under the older words. Its decode renames them
62	// by this same map, so a rename never silently drops a historical count.
63	export const LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES = Object.freeze({ preprocess: 'code-work', prework: 'code-work' });
64	
65	export function parseTaskRun(line) {
66	  const m = LINE_RE.exec(line);
67	  if (!m) return null;
68	  const [, pack, task, slotId, word] = m;
69	  const outcome = LEGACY_TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES[word] ?? word;
70	  if (!TASK_RUN_OUTCOMES.includes(outcome)) return null;
71	  return { pack, task, slotId, outcome };
72	}
73	
74	// Every record in one job log. The log is the whole job's output — this picks its
75	// own lines out of it and ignores everything else.
76	export function parseTaskRuns(text) {
77	  const out = [];
78	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
79	    const rec = parseTaskRun(line);
80	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
81	  }
82	  return out;
83	}
84	
85	// --- executor-side execution records ------------------------------------------
86	// The historical records above say what the retired slot scheduler DID with a due
87	// task; these record what an EXECUTOR SESSION did with the work it ran. Printed by executor-side code
88	// (resolve-dispatch on a terminal verdict, record-exec.mjs at convergence), they
89	// land in the session transcript, ride to the conversation-logs branch with the
90	// executor's capture step, and the usage fold counts them deterministically —
91	// the "task statuses out of the conversation logs" half of the census (owner,
92	// 2026-08-06). Same single-home rule: renderer and parser sit here together.
93	
94	export const TASK_EXEC_STATUSES = Object.freeze([
95	  // The dispatch ran to completion within its ceiling; the issue was closed.
96	  'success',
97	  // The run failed (task failure or ceiling violation); converged to needs-human.
98	  'failed',
99	  // The dispatch named a task the repo no longer carries (file gone, pack
100	  // undeclared) — the executor closed the issue as obsolete. Not a failure.
101	  'task-gone',
102	  // The dispatch was malformed (bad path shape, unparseable declaration) and was
103	  // converged to needs-human without running.
104	  'invalid',
105	]);
106	
107	export const TASK_EXEC_TAG = 'claudinite-task-exec';
108	
109	// The bracketed field is the OCCURRENCE'S IDENTITY, which is a different thing under
110	// each dispatch mechanism: a slot id (`d2026-08-06`) where slots decide what runs, and
111	// the work item's issue number (`#867`) where the queue does. `slotId` keeps its name
112	// for the fielded records that already carry one; what it must never become is a
113	// constant, since it is the only join from a record back to the work it describes.
114	export const renderTaskExec = ({ pack, task, slotId, status }) =>
115	  `${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} ${pack}/${task} [${slotId ?? 'unknown'}] ${status}`;
116	
117	const EXEC_LINE_RE = new RegExp(
118	  String.raw`(?:^|\s)${TASK_EXEC_TAG} ${VERSION} (\S+)/(\S+) \[(\S+)\] ([a-z-]+)\s*$`,
119	);
120	
121	export function parseTaskExec(line) {
122	  const m = EXEC_LINE_RE.exec(line);
123	  if (!m) return null;
124	  const [, pack, task, slotId, status] = m;
125	  if (!TASK_EXEC_STATUSES.includes(status)) return null;
126	  return { pack, task, slotId, status };
127	}
128	
129	export function parseTaskExecs(text) {
130	  const out = [];
131	  for (const line of String(text ?? '').split('\n')) {
132	    const rec = parseTaskExec(line);
133	    if (rec) out.push(rec);
134	  }
135	  return out;
136	}
